statement: Severity anchors describe what is visible in the supplied frames only. They are uncalibrated design defaults that require mechanic review before being presented as validated. They are not a mechanical diagnosis, a measurement or a safety or structural certification.

concepts.limitations: Visible surface appearance only. Extent is judged by eye relative to the panel and is not measured. Depth of corrosion, hidden corrosion and structural effect are not assessed.

anchors.description: A few tiny orange-brown specks or faint discoloration on paint or bare metal, with the paint surface still intact around them.
Several small rust spots or one small light patch of surface rust; paint is intact or only beginning to lift at the edges.
A rust patch covering a noticeable part of one panel, or a smaller patch with visibly flaking or lifting paint.
Rust covering most of a panel or spreading across a seam or edge, or any patch with heavy flaking or rough pitted texture.

Heavy rust with visible material loss such as hole-like openings, crumbling edges or missing metal. A hole-like appearance is only a flag for possible perforation (perforation_suspected); its extent and structural effect are not measured.

concepts.limitations: Visible paint surface only. Extent is judged by eye relative to the panel and is not measured. What lies beneath the paint is not assessed.

anchors.description: A few tiny isolated raised blisters in the paint.
A small cluster of blisters in one spot, paint otherwise intact.
Blisters spread across a noticeable part of one panel, or smaller clusters with some bubbles broken open.
Blistering across most of one panel, or any blistering with peeling or broken bubbles exposing the surface beneath.
Blistering with extensive peeling across several adjacent panels or along edges, with bare surface visible in many places.

concepts.limitations: Visible body shape and reflection distortion only. Extent is judged by eye relative to the panel and is not measured. Hidden damage and repair method are not assessed.

anchors.description: A very shallow, subtle distortion visible only as a slight change in the reflection.
A small shallow dent with smooth edges and intact paint.
A clearly visible dent covering a noticeable part of a panel, or a smaller dent with paint lightly cracked at the edge.
A dent covering most of a panel or spanning a panel edge, or any dent with creased edges or cracked, chipped paint.
Severe distortion with sharp creases, a folded panel, or a panel that visibly sits out of line with its neighbors.

concepts.limitations: Visible marks only. Extent is judged by eye relative to the panel and is not measured. Depth is judged from apparent color layers, not measured.

anchors.description: Faint hairline marks visible only at certain angles or in reflection.
Light scratches limited to the surface layer over a small area.
Distinct scratches running across a noticeable part of a panel, or any scratch showing a different color layer.
Scratches running across most of one panel, or long scratches showing primer-colored or bare material.
Extensive gouges or scrapes with bare material visible over a large part of a panel or across multiple panels.

concepts.limitations: Visible glass surface only. Extent is judged by eye relative to the pane and is not measured. Whether the glass is repairable or legal for use is not assessed.

anchors.description: A tiny chip or star mark with no lines radiating from it.
A small chip with one short hairline crack.
A single crack line crossing a noticeable part of the glass, or a chip with several radiating lines.
A long crack crossing a substantial part of the glass, or several separate cracks.
A network of cracks or shattered pattern across a large part of the glass, or missing glass.

concepts.limitations: Visual impression of the visible tire face only. Tread depth is not measured and the tire must be inspected in person.

anchors.description: Minor visible wear: tread pattern still looks clearly defined, with only slight rounding of tread edges.
Light uneven wear on part of the visible tread, or fine surface cracking of the rubber in a small area.
Noticeable wear: tread blocks look visibly flattened across part of the visible face, or sidewall cracking is visible.
Pronounced visible wear: tread pattern looks mostly smoothed across the visible face, a distinct band of uneven wear, or multiple sidewall cracks.
Severe visible wear or damage: tread looks largely smooth, cords or fabric are visible, or there is a visible bulge or cut in the sidewall.

concepts.limitations: Visible wetness or staining only. Extent is judged by eye relative to the component and is not measured. The fluid type, its source and whether a leak is active are not identified.

anchors.description: Faint dark or wet-looking residue on a surface, with no drips or pooling visible.
A small stained or wet-looking area, often with dirt collected around it.
A wet or streaked area covering a noticeable part of a component or surface, or any area with visible runs.
Wetness covering most of a component or surface, or any visible drips, wet trail or small puddle on a component or the ground below it.
Heavy wetness: pooled liquid or a widespread wet coating across several components or a large ground area.
